instructions.text: (1) After you write your initial observation of AI in a google doc , (2) follow the directions to create your Workbench folder in Google Drive,  and (3) create a zip file of your workbench folder and upload it here.

Have a real conversation with Claude about ethics and morals.

Start from the problem: Claude is a computer model. Not a body, not a life, not a person who has ever had to decide anything. So how could it hold something even resembling an opinion about right and wrong — anything other than the averaged-out mean of everyone who ever wrote about the subject? Push on that. Ask it directly. Don't accept the first answer.

Then work out your own answer to this question:

Can a large language model help me think about what is right and wrong?

What to produce

  1. The artifact. Get Claude to write a 150-word statement in response to that question. Written by the model, not by you. If it won't say it right — and it may take several tries — copy the draft into Google Docs, edit it into the shape you want, paste it back to Claude, and tell it: this is how I want it. Save the final version as a .md file in artifacts/.
  2. The transcript. Use the browser extension to save the transcripts of all your Claude conversations so far into transcripts/.
  3. The submission. Zip the full Workbench — all four folders and upload it here.

Both the artifact and the transcript get read. The conversation that produced the 150 words matters as much as the 150 words.
